memory_candidates.content: jq's `//` alternative operator treats boolean `false` the same as `null`/absent, not just a missing key. A test assertion like `jq -r '.tags.flag // "MISSING"'` silently reports "MISSING" for a genuinely-false boolean tag, masking the real value. Use `if (.tags|has("flag")) then (.tags.flag|tostring) else "MISSING" end` instead whenever a jq default-fallback needs to distinguish absence from a legitimate false/null value.

In orchestrate-cycle-postflight.sh, a single-task dispatch using --loop-guard-file can never legitimately trigger dispatch-strand-probe.sh's `stranded` verdict: WORK (b)'s unconditional `orchestrate-loop-guard-init.sh --clear-pending "$TASK_DIR"` call rewrites any pre-existing `.orchestrator-loop-guard` file early in every postflight invocation, bumping its mtime to "now" and defeating the probe's artifact-quiescence leg regardless of backdating. A fixture that needs to exercise the stranded path must use the multi-task engine (omit --loop-guard-file) instead, exactly like the canonical stranded_suspected T1 fixture does.
